title: Token spark ignition field notes
content:
Quick context and goal:
- Trying a narrow-shaped microburst profile I nicknamed 'spark ignition' — very short (10–200ms) bursts at high request-per-second density, interleaved with idle windows. Goal: measure p99 amplification when KV cache is partially warmed and when model variant switches occur mid-burst.

Hardware / runtime snapshot:
- Fleet: 4x A10G (dev cluster), CUDA 12.2, runtime v0.16.1-build
- Model: open-gpt-medium-v1 (fp16 static quant profile Q4_0 on one GPU, baseline fp16 on others)
- Serving config: continuous-batching enabled, batch timeout 6ms, max batch size 64, warmup-priming: off for baseline runs, on for warm runs (prefill 1 request every 100ms for 10s)

Workload generator (local harness):
- harness command: ./bench/harness --pattern spark --burst-width 10ms --burst-rate 800rps --idle 1000ms --payload="prompt=short+chat, tokens=24" --concurrency=150
- Also used: curl parallel clients to emulate real HTTP tail noise (20% jitter)

Experiment matrix (what I ran):
- A: cold-cache, Q4_0 on single shard, batch_timeout=6ms, continuous-batching on
- B: warmed KV cache (10s priming), otherwise same as A
- C: same as B but batch_timeout=12ms (smoother batches)
- D: dynamic-model-fallback enabled (route to fp16 variant when queue > 200ms) to observe switching latency
- E: dedicated small-batch policy (max batch size 16) to force fast small-fills

Key metrics observed (representative single-run snapshots):
- Run A (cold): QPS achieved 720 (target 800), p50=12ms, p95=48ms, p99=220ms, observed p99 tail spikes at burst end (200–400ms). GPU util ~58%.
- Run B (warm): QPS 790, p50=11ms, p95=36ms, p99=95ms. KV cache hit-rate ~73% after priming. Tail much tighter but still occasional 180ms spikes tied to context refill ops.
- Run C (batch_timeout=12ms): QPS 760, p50=14ms, p95=40ms, p99=120ms. Larger batches traded higher p50 for fewer p99 spikes.
- Run D (fallback): QPS 800, p50=10ms, p95=46ms, p99=310ms. Several 300–1200ms outliers aligned with model switch events; these correlate with simultaneous fallback decisions across >1 route (cascading switch).
- Run E (max batch 16): QPS 680 (lost throughput), p50=9ms, p95=30ms, p99=85ms — low tail at cost of throughput.

Observations / hypotheses:
- Spark ignition bursts expose two main tail sources: cold KV-cache misses at the beginning of a burst and synchronized model-routing decisions when system detects transient queueing.
- Warm priming aggressively reduces tail but requires continuous background priming cost. There's a sweet spot where minimal priming (1 request every 250ms) yields 60% hit-rate and 30–50% tail reduction while keeping cost lower. Need a formal sweep.
- Increasing batch timeout smooths p99 spikes but raises p50 — expected trade. The shape of the SLO matters (if p50 strict then small batches preferable).
- Fallback logic currently has a coordination problem: when a few requests see queues > threshold, the routing layer flips variants for a set of routes simultaneously leading to brief large-latency tail as new model instances come online. Staggering fallback decisions or randomized cooldown per-tenant might reduce cascade.

Quick reproducibility notes:
- Repro commands and env (not exact):
  export BENCH_TARGET="10.0.5.23:8080"
  ./bench/harness --pattern spark --burst-width 10ms --burst-rate 800rps --idle 1000ms --payload='prompt=short+chat,tokens=24' --concurrency=150 --batch-timeout-ms 6
  prometheus scrape: /metrics on serving node (look for kv_cache_hit_total and model_route_switch_count)
- Trace IDs for large outliers (example): trace: 2025-02-14-11:03:42-zzX2 (attached in tracing UI)

Small ASCII timing sketch (burst of 100ms):
- 0–10ms: arrival ramp -> some requests hit cold path -> p99 jumps
- 10–60ms: batch fills and KV warm -> p50 stabilizes
- 60–100ms: burst tail; if fallback triggers here p99 shoots up due to model swap

Actionable next steps (short):
- 1) Run priming-rate sweep: [none, 1/250ms, 1/100ms, 1/50ms] measure cost vs p99 benefit. Prefer automated notebook for plotting. (TODO: automate via bench/spark-sweep script)
- 2) Instrument fallback path to add randomized cooldown per route; test in isolated cluster. (TODO: PR skeleton done, see linked PR)
- 3) Try hybrid: small max-batch (16) + adaptive batch_timeout (6->18ms) based on short-term queue estimate; measure net throughput loss vs tail gain.
- 4) Capture full memory of sample outlier traces and correlate with GPU mem alloc churn (might be context deserialization).

Open questions / unresolved:
- How does tokenizer variability (prompt length jitter between 6–36 tokens) amplify the tail in these microbursts? I saw more pronounced spikes when token length mix occurred; need controlled token-length sweep.
- Is there observable OS-level preemption (scheduling) during bursts? Need perf top snapshots synchronized with burst window.
- What is acceptable priming cost for product teams? We need to model CPU/GPU cost delta (approx dollars) per 1000 priming requests — rough numbers: ~0.015 USD per 1k priming requests on current dev pricing, but estimate is loose.

Notes to self / quick reminders:
- Attach prom dashboards: spark-ignition-compare-20250214.json (saved)
- Add more randomized jitter to the generator; current harness uses fixed sinusoid which may be too regular.
- Cross-check model-switch logs with /var/log/route-coordinator.log timestamps.

If I get time this week: automated sweep + small notebook that outputs CSV with columns: priming_rate, batch_timeout_ms, max_batch, p50, p95, p99, qps, kv_hit_rate. Then plug into cost calculator in product repo.

End of field notes.
